title: Top 5 Deadliest Animals to Humans
hook: These animals kill more people than any others, and number one is tiny.

items.name: Crocodiles
items.line: Crocodiles are behind roughly a thousand human deaths every year, mostly in Africa and Asia.

items.name: Assassin Bugs
items.line: Assassin bugs spread Chagas disease, which kills around ten thousand people a year.

items.name: Dogs
items.line: Dogs cause almost all of the fifty nine thousand rabies deaths each year.

items.name: Snakes
items.line: Snakebites kill between eighty one thousand and one hundred thirty eight thousand people a year, says the World Health Organization.

items.name: Mosquitoes
items.line: Mosquitoes spread malaria, which alone kills over half a million people every single year.

outro: Which animal scares you the most? Tell me below.
description: The animals responsible for the most human deaths each year, based on World Health Organization estimates.
sources: World Health Organization fact sheets (malaria, snakebite envenoming, rabies, Chagas disease)

title: Countries Where the Most People Use AI
hook: In one country, seven out of ten adults already use AI. Can you guess which?

items.name: France
items.line: In France, nearly forty eight percent of working age adults now use AI tools.

items.name: Ireland
items.line: Ireland edges ahead at about forty eight and a half percent, helped by its big tech industry.

items.name: Norway
items.line: Norway takes third with just under forty nine percent of adults using AI.

items.name: Singapore
items.line: Singapore jumps way ahead, with over sixty three percent of adults using AI.

items.name: United Arab Emirates
items.line: The United Arab Emirates leads the world, with seventy percent of working age people using AI.

outro: Where do you think your country ranks? Comment below.
description: Countries ranked by the share of working-age people who use AI tools, from Microsoft's AI Diffusion Report for the first quarter of 2026.
sources: Visual Capitalist — Mapped: AI Adoption by Country in 2026

title: The 5 Tallest Buildings in the World
hook: Number one is so tall you can watch the sunset twice in one day.

items.name: Ping An Finance Center
items.line: Ping An Finance Center in Shenzhen, China, rises five hundred ninety nine meters.

items.name: Makkah Clock Tower
items.line: The Makkah Royal Clock Tower in Saudi Arabia reaches six hundred one meters and has one of the world's largest clock faces.

items.name: Shanghai Tower
items.line: The twisting Shanghai Tower stands six hundred thirty two meters tall.

items.name: Merdeka 118
items.line: Merdeka one eighteen in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, reaches six hundred seventy nine meters.

items.name: Burj Khalifa
items.line: Dubai's Burj Khalifa towers eight hundred twenty eight meters, almost one hundred fifty meters taller than second place.

outro: Would you dare go to the top of number one?
description: The tallest completed buildings in the world, ranked by architectural height (Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat).
sources: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) Skyscraper Center

title: The 5 Largest Countries in the World
hook: Number one is bigger than the surface of Pluto.

items.name: Brazil
items.line: Brazil covers about eight and a half million square kilometers, nearly half of South America.

items.name: China
items.line: China spans about nine point six million square kilometers but uses just one time zone.

items.name: United States
items.line: The United States covers about nine point eight million square kilometers, including Alaska.

items.name: Canada
items.line: Canada has nearly ten million square kilometers and the longest coastline on Earth.

items.name: Russia
items.line: Russia is a massive seventeen million square kilometers, stretching across eleven time zones.

outro: Which country would you want to explore first?
description: The world's biggest countries ranked by total area (land and water).

title: The 5 Fastest Animals on the Planet
hook: Number one moves faster than a Formula One car.

items.name: Pronghorn
items.line: The pronghorn hits about eighty eight kilometers per hour and can hold its speed for miles.

items.name: Cheetah
items.line: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, sprinting over one hundred kilometers per hour in seconds.

items.name: Free-Tailed Bat
items.line: The Brazilian free tailed bat was clocked at around one hundred sixty kilometers per hour in level flight.

items.name: Golden Eagle
items.line: A diving golden eagle can reach about two hundred forty kilometers per hour.

items.name: Peregrine Falcon
items.line: The peregrine falcon dives at over three hundred twenty kilometers per hour, with a record near three hundred ninety.

outro: Did you expect a bird at number one?
description: The fastest animals in the world, ranked by top recorded speed. Speeds are approximate and vary by study.
sources: Royal Society Open Science (2016) bat flight study

title: The 5 Deepest Places in the Ocean
hook: Number one is deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

items.name: Kuril-Kamchatka Trench
items.line: The Kuril Kamchatka Trench off Russia plunges about nine thousand six hundred meters.

items.name: Kermadec Trench
items.line: New Zealand's Kermadec Trench reaches about ten thousand meters down.

items.name: Philippine Trench
items.line: The Philippine Trench sinks about ten thousand five hundred meters, just off Mindanao.

items.name: Tonga Trench
items.line: The Tonga Trench's Horizon Deep reaches about ten thousand eight hundred meters.

items.name: Mariana Trench
items.line: The Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep is about eleven kilometers down, where pressure is a thousand times stronger than at the surface.

outro: Would you ever go down there in a submarine?
description: The deepest ocean trenches on Earth, ranked by their deepest measured point. Depths are approximate.

title: The 5 Biggest Planets in Our Solar System
hook: You could fit more than a thousand Earths inside number one.

items.name: Earth
items.line: Earth is about twelve thousand seven hundred kilometers wide, the biggest rocky planet.

items.name: Neptune
items.line: Neptune is nearly four times wider than Earth and has the fastest winds in the solar system.

items.name: Uranus
items.line: Uranus is just a bit wider than Neptune and spins tipped over on its side.

items.name: Saturn
items.line: Saturn is over nine times wider than Earth and light enough that it would float in water.

items.name: Jupiter
items.line: Jupiter is so huge that more than thirteen hundred Earths could fit inside it.

outro: Which planet would you visit first?
description: The largest planets in our solar system ranked by diameter, using NASA figures.

title: The 5 Highest Mountains on Earth
hook: All five are in Asia, and number one is still growing.

items.name: Makalu
items.line: Makalu, on the Nepal China border, rises eight thousand four hundred eighty five meters.

items.name: Lhotse
items.line: Lhotse stands eight thousand five hundred sixteen meters, right next door to Everest.

items.name: Kangchenjunga
items.line: Kangchenjunga reaches eight thousand five hundred eighty six meters and was once thought to be the tallest.

items.name: K2
items.line: K2 is eight thousand six hundred eleven meters, and far deadlier to climb than Everest.

items.name: Mount Everest
items.line: Mount Everest stands eight thousand eight hundred forty nine meters and still rises a few millimeters every year.

outro: Would you ever try to climb number one?
description: The highest mountains in the world ranked by elevation above sea level.
sources: Nepal and China joint survey (2020) for Everest

title: The 5 Largest Deserts in the World
hook: The biggest desert on Earth isn't hot at all.

items.name: Gobi Desert
items.line: The Gobi in Mongolia and China covers about one point three million square kilometers.

items.name: Arabian Desert
items.line: The Arabian Desert spans about two point three million square kilometers.

items.name: Sahara Desert
items.line: The Sahara is the biggest hot desert, about the size of the entire United States.

items.name: Arctic Desert
items.line: The Arctic counts as a desert because it gets so little rain or snow, covering about fourteen million square kilometers.

items.name: Antarctic Desert
items.line: Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth, at about fourteen million square kilometers of ice.

outro: Did you know Antarctica was a desert? Comment yes or no.
description: The world's largest deserts by area. A desert is defined by low precipitation, not heat.
